title: Mexico eSIM: phone-line ID rules and data | Magic eSIM
description: What Mexico's new phone-line identification rules cover, and plans that also cover the United States and Canada. Online payment is not available yet.
lead: Data for a trip to Mexico, with what the country's new phone-line rules actually say and regional plans that also cover the United States and Canada.

sections.h2: Mexico's phone-line identification rules: who they apply to
paragraphs: Guidelines from Mexico's telecoms regulator, the CRT, in force since 9 December 2025, require every mobile line provided by a Mexican licensed company or reseller to be linked to an identified holder. Under a June 2026 amendment, lines that are still not linked are switched off in stages between August and December 2026, according to the last digit of the number; a line that has been switched off can still call emergency and citizen-service numbers and its own company's customer service.

If you buy a Mexican SIM or a Mexican eSIM during your stay, you identify yourself with your passport, with a CURP (Mexico's population registry code) issued to foreigners, or with a visitor or resident card from the National Migration Institute that carries a CURP. Under the rules, the company records only your name, country of origin, passport number or CURP, the phone number and the result of the check.

Phones visiting on international roaming are a separate case. The guidelines leave it to the CRT to define, once the 2026 World Cup is over, how lines that use international roaming in Mexico are to be linked. This page makes no claim about how such arrangements treat a phone or plan from abroad.

Mexico City's airport, AICM, offers free Wi-Fi called #AICM_FREE_WIFI in both terminals, from the public areas to the last waiting rooms before boarding. You connect with one click, and after two hours you accept the terms again to carry on.
Mexico has a single emergency number, 911. It is worth noting it alongside your hotel address before you land.

sections.h2: Mexico alone, or a trip into the United States and Canada
paragraphs: Local plans cover Mexico alone, which suits a trip that stays inside the country. Daily plans give you a set amount of data per day, which fits a long road trip where every day looks much the same. If the journey continues into the United States or Canada, regional plans that include Mexico also cover both countries.

Before choosing, confirm that your phone supports eSIM and is not locked to your home network with the [compatibility guide](/en/guides/compatibility/), and see the [activation guide](/en/guides/activation/) for what decides when a plan's term begins.

faq.q: Do I have to register my phone in Mexico as a tourist?
faq.a: The identification rules apply to lines provided by Mexican companies: if you buy a Mexican SIM or eSIM, you link it to yourself, for example with your passport. For lines on international roaming, the guidelines leave the arrangements for the regulator to define after the 2026 World Cup, and this page makes no claim about them.

faq.q: Can I buy a Mexican SIM with a passport?
faq.a: Yes. The rules accept a passport, a CURP for foreigners, or a visitor or resident card that carries a CURP.

faq.q: Is there a plan that covers Mexico, the United States and Canada?
faq.a: Yes: regional plans that include Mexico also cover the United States and Canada.

faq.q: Is there free Wi-Fi at Mexico City airport?
faq.a: Yes. AICM offers #AICM_FREE_WIFI in both terminals; sessions last up to two hours, after which you accept the terms again.

faq.q: What is the emergency number in Mexico?
faq.a: 911 is Mexico's single number for emergency calls.
